name: Exa
summary: A search engine built for programs: embeddings-based web retrieval, find-similar, and contents returned ready to feed a model.
description:
Exa indexes the web so retrieval can be semantic rather than keyword-only: query by meaning, ask for pages similar to a known good one, categorise results by intent, and fetch the contents in a form you can paste into a context window. AI products use it as the grounding layer when the built-in search of a model is not enough.

It is still a search engine, with a search engine's failure modes — coverage gaps, recency trade-offs, and pages that exist in the index but are gone by the time you cite them. Per-query pricing is easy to underestimate inside an agent loop that searches several times per task.
